thread:
Alex: Quick sync — we need to lock down SLO tiers + sizing heuristics for Dedicated capacity PRD. Proposing: 3 SLO buckets (platinum/gold/silver), burst-credit for short spikes, cache warm-up behavior, and autoscale hysteresis. Need clear acceptance criteria and edge-case rules before we ship.

Maya: +1 on tiers. can we put numbers on p99/p95 targets? also curious how burst-credit interacts with reserved pools.

Prithvi: Suggestion — define per-GPU ‘steady throughput’ and separate ‘burst throughput’ window. steady = what we provision for committed capacity. burst uses credits drawn from short window (e.g., 5m) with soft throttling after credit exhausted.

Sam: We should also call out KV cache cold-start impact. Example: on long-tail requests, first 5 requests will be ~2x latency until KV warmed. PRD should include cache-warmup mitigation (prefetch or synthetic warmers).

Jordan: From infra POV, need explicit circuit-breaker thresholds: drop to silver model variant or enqueue + 429 policy. Otherwise risk noisy neighbor on Dedicated pools. Also include fallback routing to other regions.

Katie: A few concrete numbers to start discussion:
- Platinum: p99 < 80ms, success rate >= 99.95%
- Gold: p95 < 120ms, success rate >= 99.9%
- Silver: p90 < 200ms, success rate >= 99.0%
These assume steady-state per-GPU throughput estimates (see below).

Prithvi: throughput heuristics (ballpark):
- small context chat (<=512 tokens): 380-420 reqs/s per A100-like GPU (batching on)
- medium contexts (512-2k): 120-200 reqs/s per GPU
- long contexts (>2k): 20-80 reqs/s per GPU
We should include a matrix in PRD linking model family + quantization -> throughput.

Maya: On autoscale: define hysteresis windows so we don’t oscillate. e.g., trigger scale-up if 90th percentile CPU/GPU utilization > 78% for 60s; scale-down only if <50% for 10m. Also allow manual override for committed pools.

Alex: +1. Also want explicit acceptance criteria for launch (PRD ready):
- Performance: all tiers meet latency & success targets over 24h simulated workload (including KV cold paths)
- Stability: no more than 1 incident (SEV >=2) in canary 48h
- Cost: per-token cost estimate documented with sensitivity for batching & quantization
- Rollout plan: canary traffic, fallback policy, and post-mortem checklist

Jordan: Edge cases to call out in PRD:
- Model oversubscription when customer pins large models -> autoscale inability if infra quota hits, need graceful denial with clear error & SRE alert
- Network partitions between control plane and Private deployments -> local fallback or degraded mode behavior
- Long-tail adversarial workloads (very long context + repeated KV miss) -> apply per-customer rate-limits and isolated pools

Sam: For tests, we should add an evaluation harness that replays customer prompt traces including head-of-line spikes and synthetic long-context queries. Include warmup scenarios for KV.

Prithvi: Quick config example to include in PRD for product & infra teams:
```yaml
slo_buckets:
  platinum:
    p99_latency_ms: 80
    success_rate_pct: 99.95
    steady_throughput_per_gpu: 400
  gold:
    p95_latency_ms: 120
    success_rate_pct: 99.9
    steady_throughput_per_gpu: 350
  silver:
    p90_latency_ms: 200
    success_rate_pct: 99.0
    steady_throughput_per_gpu: 200
burst_credit:
  window_seconds: 300
  credit_rate_multiplier: 2.0 # can sustain 2x for short bursts
autoscale:
  scale_up_trigger:
    util_pct: 78
    sustained_seconds: 60
  scale_down_trigger:
    util_pct: 50
    sustained_seconds: 600
cache:
  kv_warmup_tokens: 2000
  prefetch_enabled: true
```

Maya: Love the YAML. Two asks: 1) add clear rollback criteria for canary (e.g., >0.5% regression in quality metrics OR >10% latency regression), 2) call out how quantization reduces latency vs potential accuracy regressions and where to pin model variants per tier.

Alex: Good call. Add rollout rollback rules and QA gating. Also need acceptance criteria for fallback: if primary tier cannot be met for >3m, we should auto-failover to next compatible model variant or region and emit a customer-visible notice + billing adjustment flag.

Jordan: Ops question — how do we represent burst credits in billing? Option A: no billing change, treat as included burst for reserved pools (preferred). Option B: bill overage at higher per-token rate. Need finance input.

Katie: For PRD, include a section: "Billing & customer expectations" describing both options and recommended default (Option A for committed customers, Option B opt-in for smaller customers).

Prithvi: Edge-case: what if burst-credit abused by hammering small requests continuously? We need sliding-window enforcement + per-customer token burn rate thresholds, and a soft 429/queue strategy.

Sam: QA notes: create synthetic load generator that mimics token-length mix and includes KV miss ratio. Run 3x 24h runs to validate 99.95% targets for platinum. Document the test configs in PRD.

Alex: Action items:
- I'll draft the PRD with the YAML, acceptance criteria, rollout & rollback rules, and test plan. Target: end of day Friday. @Maya @Prithvi @Jordan please review and flag any hard blockers.

Maya: I can review tomorrow morning.

Jordan: I'll add ops runbook snippets and circuit-breaker behavior by EOD Thursday.

Prithvi: I'll add throughput matrix per model family + quantization notes.

DeployBot: Reminder: meeting scheduled — Dedicated Capacity PRD kickoff Thu 09:30 PST — invites sent. :calendar:

Katie: Thanks — looks actionable. :thumbsup:

Alex: Great, thanks everyone. I'll ping the thread when draft is up.
